To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TD-CIMS can measure N2O5 with an unheating inlet and that a significant daytime signal of N2O 5 + NO3 is observed in Hong Kong, which is likely caused by chemical interferences.

1) the TD-CIMS can be a very useful instrument to measure N2O5 under a low NOx environment, 2) peroxy acetyl nitrates (PAN) contribute to measurable signals at m/z 62 amu and this interference increases significantly with co-existense of NO2, 3) nitric acid (HONO) has little interference to the TD-CIMS detection of N2 O5/NO3, 4) evidence for the

daytime signals of N2 O 5 + NO 3 at 62 am u in a TD-C I M S were found to be significantly larger than expected, and this phenomenon could be attributed to chemical interferences, elevated daytime N 2 O5, or both.

the daytime signals of N2 O5 and NO ₃ at 62 am u in a TD-C IMS are most likely the combined results of chemical interferences and real atmospheric phenomena.
the TD-CIMS signal at 62 m/z is not a direct measurement of the ambient N2O 5 and NO3 concentrations in a high NO 2 environment.
there are large daytime signals of N2 O5 + NO3 at 62 am u in a TD-C IMS, but the exact origin and contribution from the inter-fering chemicals are yet to be fully understood and quantified.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 62 amu signal is not a reliable indicator of N2O 5 and NO3 concentrations in urban environments with high NOx concentrations.
the daytime N2O 5 + NO3 signals observed in our TD-CIM S are likely to be overestimated by 30–50%, but a significant portion of these signals are still real.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the daytime N2O 5 + NO 3 signal at 62amu in the TD-CIM S is not a chemical interference but a real atmospheric phenomenon.
daytime N2O 5 + NO3 signals in the range of a few hundred pptv are real, and that daytime N2 O5 + NO3 concentrations can be much higher than the nighttime values.
